patches.explication: The application takes user input from the 'q' parameter in the URL and displays it directly on the page without any sanitization or encoding. This allows an attacker to craft a malicious link containing a script tag; when a victim clicks this link, the browser executes the script, which can lead to session theft or unauthorized actions on the user's behalf.
patches.solution: Use the htmlspecialchars() function to encode special HTML characters, ensuring that the browser treats the input as literal text rather than executable code.
patches.code_vulnerable:
<form action="xss.php" method="get">
<input name="q" value=""/>
<button type="submit">Search</button>
</form>
<?php echo $_GET['q']; ?>
patches.code_corrige:
<form action="xss.php" method="get">
<input name="q" value=""/>
<button type="submit">Search</button>
</form>
<?php if (isset($_GET['q'])) { echo htmlspecialchars($_GET['q'], ENT_QUOTES, 'UTF-8'); } ?>

patches.explication: The application accepts user input from the form and likely inserts it directly into a SQL query string on the server. This allows an attacker to input special SQL characters, such as ' OR '1'='1', which modifies the logic of the query to always be true, potentially allowing them to bypass authentication or access unauthorized database records.
patches.solution: Use PDO prepared statements with parameterized queries to ensure that user input is treated strictly as data and not as executable code.
patches.code_vulnerable:
<form action="submit.php" method="post">
<label for="name">Name</label>
<input id="name" name="name"/>
<label for="email">Email</label>
<input id="email" name="email"/>
<button type="submit">Submit</button>
</form>
patches.code_corrige:
<?php
// Database configuration
$host = 'localhost';
$db   = 'app_database';
$user = 'db_user';
$pass = 'db_password';
$charset = 'utf8mb4';

$dsn = "mysql:host=$host;dbname=$db;charset=$charset";
$options = [
    PDO::ATTR_ERRMODE            => PDO::ERRMODE_EXCEPTION,
    PDO::ATTR_DEFAULT_FETCH_MODE => PDO::FETCH_ASSOC,
    PDO::ATTR_EMULATE_PREPARES   => false,
];

try {
    $pdo = new PDO($dsn, $user, $pass, $options);
} catch (\PDOException $e) {
    die("Database connection failed.");
}

if ($_SERVER["REQUEST_METHOD"] == "POST") {
    $name = $_POST['name'] ?? '';
    $email = $_POST['email'] ?? '';

    // Using a prepared statement to prevent SQL Injection
    $stmt = $pdo->prepare("SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = :name AND email = :email");
    $stmt->execute(['name' => $name, 'email' => $email]);
    $user = $stmt->fetch();

    if ($user) {
        echo "User found: " . htmlspecialchars($user['name']);
    } else {
        echo "Invalid input or user not found.";
    }
}
?>

patches.explication: The provided HTML form collects an email address and sends it to 'submit.php'. The vulnerability occurs on the server side when that email input is inserted directly into a SQL query string without validation or escaping. An attacker can use a payload like "' OR '1'='1' --" to change the query's logic, making the condition always true, which allows them to bypass authentication or extract all user data from the database.
patches.solution: Use PDO prepared statements with parameterized queries to ensure that user input is treated strictly as data and never as executable SQL code.
patches.code_vulnerable:
<form action="submit.php" method="post">
<label for="name">Name</label>
<input id="name" name="name"/>
<label for="email">Email</label>
<input id="email" name="email"/>
<button type="submit">Submit</button>
</form>
patches.code_corrige:
<form action="submit.php" method="post">
<label for="name">Name</label>
<input id="name" name="name"/>
<label for="email">Email</label>
<input id="email" name="email"/>
<label for="password">Password</label>
<input id="password" name="password" type="password"/>
<button type="submit">Submit</button>
</form>

<?php
// submit.php - Secure implementation
$host = 'localhost';
$db   = 'web_app';
$user = 'db_user';
$pass = 'secure_password';
$charset = 'utf8mb4';

$dsn = "mysql:host=$host;dbname=$db;charset=$charset";
$options = [
    PDO::ATTR_ERRMODE            => PDO::ERRMODE_EXCEPTION,
    PDO::ATTR_DEFAULT_FETCH_MODE => PDO::FETCH_ASSOC,
    PDO::ATTR_EMULATE_PREPARES   => false,
];

try {
    $pdo = new PDO($dsn, $user, $pass, $options);

    // Use null coalescing operator to handle missing POST data
    $email = $_POST['email'] ?? '';
    $password = $_POST['password'] ?? '';

    // 1. Use Prepared Statements to prevent SQL Injection
    $stmt = $pdo->prepare("SELECT id, password_hash FROM users WHERE email = ?");
    $stmt->execute([$email]);
    $user = $stmt->fetch();

    // 2. Use password_verify to check hashed passwords (stored via password_hash)
    if ($user && password_verify($password, $user['password_hash'])) {
        echo "Authentication successful.";
    } else {
        echo "Invalid email or password.";
    }
} catch (\PDOException $e) {
    // Log error and show generic message to user
    error_log($e->getMessage());
    exit("A system error occurred. Please try again later.");
}
?>
